text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime minister pledges not to yield to Palestinian Authority demands.
- Beit El settlers to discuss expansion with Defence Ministry.
- Shas party spiritual leader Rabbi Ovadia Yosef tells Shas cabinet ministers not to vote for Hebron deal.
- Israeli-Arab lifestyle change may create old-age home boom.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke our long-built trust in six months.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton pressuring Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to complete deal before their visits to U.S. after presidential inauguration on Jan 20.
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai committed to expanding Beit El settlement.
- Contacts to locate missing Israeli airman Ron Arad halted, against background of deterioration in German-Iranian relations.
- Charge in Israel: Mubarak "torpedoing" completion of Hebron deal. Today is a year to the liquidation of Hamas master bombmaker "The Engineer". Security forces prepared.
- Treasury approved transfer of 20 million shekels from pension fund to Bank Leumi in violation of regulations.
- Difficulties in Hebron negotiations. Shas threatens to vote against the agreement. Signs of a tie in the government.
